texts.preamble: Gujrat Cooperative Milk Marketing ... vs State Of M.P. on 24 September, 2025 Author: Milind Ramesh Phadke Bench: Milind Ramesh Phadke Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Gwl:24082 1 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh At Gwalior Before Hon'Ble Shri Justice Milind Ramesh Phadke On The 24 th Of September, 2025 Misc. Criminal Case No. 6428 of 2011 Gujrat Cooperative Milk Marketing Federation Ltd. And Others Versus State Of M.P. And Others Appearance: Shri Mahesh Goyal - Advocate for the petitioners.
texts.facts: 2. The short facts of the case are that complainant/respondent no.1 had filed a complaint before Judicial Magistrate First Class Gwalior which was registered as Case No1039/10 for convicting the petitioners alongwith others for the offences under section 7(i), 7(ii)/16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 alleging that on 18.07.2009, the food inspector, complainant, intercepted truck no. MH04 GA 0439 of M/s Sherawali Roadways, Bhopal, which was allegedly carrying Ghee of various brands allegedly manufactured by different manufacturers. The said alleged stocks were seized and kept at M/s Shiva, a Carrier Transport, Transport Nagar, Gwalior on account of absence of the owner as the driver of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:24082 2 MCRC-6428-2011 truck did not produce any invoice from GCMMF ltd., Mother Dairy Gandhinagar or any of the authorized whole sale dealer / dealers of GCMMF. It was further submitted that on 19.08.2009 at about 5:30PM, on the oral instruction of Shri Ved Prakash, ADM Gwalior, the complainant remained present at Shiva Road Carrier Transport Nagar, Gwalior. One Mukul Anand Gujrat Cooperative Milk Marketing ... vs State Of M.P. on 24 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114807610/ 1 S/o Stayendra Anand Age-29 years, R/o F10, Panjabi Bagh, Raisen Road Bhopal came as a representative with the authority letter of Amrit Trading Company. Infront of them seized articles were opened and on inspection, the Jars of Amul, Sneh Gopala, Krishna Ghee Brands were found. On the basis of suspicion, samples were taken and the proceedings of sending the sample for tests were completed. It was further averred that the seized articles were found adulterated, which is a punishable offence, upon which tt was prayed that the respondents be punished under section 7/16 of PFA Act. Consequently, cognizance was taken for commission of offence under Sections 7 and 16 of the PFA Act against the petitioners.
texts.arguments: 3. The contention of learned counsel for the petitioners is that the petitioners are bona fide manufacturers of dairy products under the registered brand "Amul," and none of the seized articles in question were manufactured or distributed by them. It is submitted that the seized articles were spurious and misbranded in the name of "Amul" by unauthorized persons, and the petitioners had no privity of contract with the transporter or the co-accused. It is further urged that Rule 12-A of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 obliges every manufacturer, distributor or dealer selling an article of food to supply a warranty in Form VI-A or issue a cash memo or bill, but in the present case, no such document were produced by the complainant to show that the present petitioner had sold or distributed the impugned ghee to any dealer and in that process, it was being transported. Hence, fastening of liability on the petitioners in the absence of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:24082 3 MCRC-6428-2011 cogent material is wholly unsustainable in law. 4. Per contra, learned counsel for the State submits that adulterated and misbranded Ghee jars were found in the truck, including those labeled as "Amul," and the Public Analyst's report confirmed misbranding. The Magistrate, upon considering the complaint and documents, rightly found sufficient ground to proceed under Sections 7 and 16 of the PFA Act. It is argued that at the stage of cognizance, a detailed appreciation of defence is not required. 7. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pepsi Foods Ltd. v. Special Judicial Magistrate (1998) 5 SCC 749 has observed that summoning of an accused in a criminal case is a serious matter and the Magistrate must apply his judicial mind to the facts of the case and the law applicable.
